title: All things food and culture from New York, Milan, and Lagos: Ugo Ugochukwu on his Hometown
excerpt:
2026 champion Ugo Ugochukwu's plans for next year are already taking shape, and while he is looking to the future, we recently sat down with him to talk about the past.

The Campos Racing driver talked about growing up in New York, while also having roots in Italy and Nigeria. From food to music, he takes the best part from each country.

NEW YORK

“I obviously grew up in New York City, so it’s quite a chaotic place, I'm sure most people would see it like that.

“I think for me, growing up there was a bit more normal. You just kind of get used to it, you get used to all the noise and that stuff doesn't really affect you.

“But moving out, I have obviously lived in Italy for at least half of my life now as well, and that's a very different environment, much quieter.

“I grew up on the Lower East Side, so I'd say it's a bit quieter than Midtown. It's not as busy, but not as busy for New York, it's still lots of people.

Ugochukwu grew up in New York but has family in Italy and Nigeria

“But I used to do normal stuff growing up. I went to school and I have strong memories of being in the park with friends and mates and just hanging around, being a kid, nothing crazy.

“We’d play football, go to tennis, and on weekends, movies, I enjoy going to the movies quite a bit.

“New York has quite a lot of culture, everyone knows I like my music, and a lot of great musicians have come from there.”

‘I feel very honoured’ – Zhenrui Chi on stepping up to Formula 3 with MP Motorsport

Colnaghi aiming to maintain Campos’ status as double champions in 2027

MILAN AND LAGOS

“Of course Milan is a little bit different. Like I said, a bit quieter. I think for me, obviously, I started racing in Europe quite young. But it was not such a huge transition for me.

“Half of my family is Italian, so I've been coming to Italy since I was very young, and obviously, I speak the language and I've got a few family friends.

“So for me, obviously, it was pretty easy to switch back and forth. I still do between New York and Italy, and I stay there during the main season. But then, of course, I go back to New York during the off season and get to go back home a little bit for a few months.

Ugochukwu spoke about his favourite food to eat when back in New York

“I've been back to Nigeria more often before than in the last few years because I haven't been so many times. But it's always cool to go back there and to see my family in Lagos.”

DIFFERENT FOOD CHOICES

“I'm going to be real, I'm eating Italian food in New York. So that's exactly the same, whether I'm in New York or in Italy. But I think New York is quite unique because you get all types of cuisine.

“I do have to say my favourite cuisine in New York has to be Chinese takeaway. So it’s not a posh, fancy restaurant. But Chinese takeaway is definitely my favourite thing to order. Probably a little bit like a cheat meal.

“But Italian food, I'd probably say the best is pasta. I really like, more specifically, Poli Ragu pasta. I'd probably say that's my favourite one. Nigerian food I'd say just jollof rice, chicken, and plantain. Keep it simple.”

title: ‘I feel very honoured’ – Zhenrui Chi on stepping up to Formula 3 with MP Motorsport
excerpt:
Zhenrui Chi says he is proud to be stepping up to Formula 3 in 2027 and he has already laid out what his goals for the upcoming season will be.

The Italian driver graduates to F3 after his first full year in the Formula Regional European Championship where he finished eighth in the Championship racing for MP Motorsport.

Chi also has previous success in the 2025 Italian F4 Championship where he won one race and achieved four podiums in total.

The Aston Martin Driver Academy member now gets a chance to race in F3, and he revealed his pride at doing so with MP.

“I feel very honoured and proud to be racing in F3, especially with this kind of a team,” said Chi. “They've done really good this season, so I'm looking forward to it.

Chi shared his first impressions of the Formula 3 car

“Obviously, I still have a lot of things to learn, jumping from Regional to F3, but working with a team that I did already for a year will be much better.

“I would say this is definitely a much better car in almost every aspect. I like it a lot and I think I'll be enjoying driving this car.”

Colnaghi aiming to maintain Campos’ status as double champions in 2027

Clerot aiming for the title next season after ending 2026 on a high

Chi is currently taking part in the 2026 Macau Grand Prix and he has already started his preparations for the 2027 campaign.

The 17-year-old talked about the areas he feels he needs to work on ahead of the opening race weekend in Sakhir and the rest of the season.

Chi talked about what he feels he needs to do to be competitive next season

“For me, I would like to focus more on myself,” said Chi. “I just want to focus on each corner, maximising every corner, and being more consistent.

“I think if I achieve that for every corner, the results will definitely come. So it's more like focusing on my driving.

'Familiarity a strength for us': Enzo Deligny on re-signing with Van Amersfoort Racing

Wheldon aiming to ‘fight for the championship’ in debut F3 season

“I think the mental side is one of the most important because you have to always stay confident as there's only a few laps in quali, so you need to know very well what to do while staying calm.”

On what he has to do to make sure he is there fighting at the front, Chi said: “Just again, working on myself mentally and physically, maximising each corner and just focus corner by corner and we'll be there.”

title: Colnaghi aiming to maintain Campos’ status as double champions in 2027
excerpt:
Mattia Colnaghi is aiming for both titles in 2027 with Campos Racing

Mattia Colnaghi is returning for a second season in Formula 3 in 2027 but doing so in new colours, as he joins the reigning champions Campos Racing.

The Argentine had a rookie year of two halves, scoring just one point through the first five rounds.

However, Colnaghi’s results improved in the second part of the season, achieving several points finishes, including finishing fourth places in four consecutive races in Spa-Francorchamps and Budapest.

Colnaghi ended the year 13th in the Drivers’ Standings with 54 points and now returns with a new team for 2027.

Speaking at the Jerez post-season test last month, the 18-year-old said: “I’m feeling good, and I am really happy to join Campos for 2027.

Colnaghi is getting to know his new team ahead of the 2027 campaign

“Obviously, they've proven that they are the ones to beat, at least in F3, winning both titles. So I am really happy to be part of the team and happy to start working with them. I am looking forward to next year.”

When asked whether how he intends to build on last year going into next season, Colnaghi highlighted a key area that he needs to improve on.

Clerot aiming for the title next season after ending 2026 on a high

'Familiarity a strength for us': Enzo Deligny on re-signing with Van Amersfoort Racing

“I think it's just mainly using the learning experience from last year in all cases,” he said. “In terms of consistency and in terms of obviously improving the results to get some podiums and wins.

“So I just need to maximise everything. I think consistency is the biggest part of it, so looking into that, and how we can do it.”

This will be Colnaghi’s first season racing with Campos in any category, but having competed against them for several years now, he has a fair idea of the team.

Colnaghi is aiming for consistency and to fight for wins and podiums next year

The Red Bull Junior has raced against the Spanish outfit since stepping up to single seaters in 2024, and says so far, he has fitted in seamlessly.

“There are a few things new to get used to,” he said. “This will be a challenge and has been a challenge already. But overall, I think it has been quite easy to get used to.

Wheldon aiming to ‘fight for the championship’ in debut F3 season

‘It’s a great honour’ – Dion Gowda on stepping up to F3 with LN4 Fusion

“It is a Spanish team, and I've raced in Spanish championships. I've known them for quite some time already, so it's been quite good.”

Colnaghi stepped up to Formula 3 this year with a strong resume in single seaters, having won the 2024 Spanish F4 and 2025 Eurocup-3 Championships. The aim for the Argentine driver is returning to winning ways in 2027.

“The ultimate goal is to obviously become champion,” he said. “I want to maintain the Campos status as Teams’ and Drivers’ champion. I think that's the only way we can go next year.”

title: Clerot aiming for the title next season after ending 2026 on a high
excerpt:
Pedro Clerot is back not only in Formula 3 for another season but also with Rodin Motorsport and is optimistic that it will lead to a title challenge in 2027.

The Brazilian was one of the standout drivers in 2026, finishing sixth in the Championship Standings as a rookie.

Clerot achieved five podiums, including a Feature Race victory at the final round in Madrid, and he is hopeful that fine end to the season can put him and the team in a good position for next year.

“I think we ended 2026 on a good note,” said Clerot. “Madrid was a very good round and we delivered some very strong performances, both me and the team, and I think we really showed what we can do.

“So I'm just excited. The calendar looks quite cool, and I'm very happy with the new tracks. There are some places I've really wanted to go my whole life and now I get the chance to go.

Clerot was back in the car for Rodin at the post-season tests in Jerez and Barcelona

“I'm looking forward to the first three tracks in a row, which I don't mind. I've had really good feelings the last year, both in Monaco with my first podium and then obviously Madrid with the win. I'm just excited.”

Clerot gets to continue with Rodin having built a strong relationship with the team during his rookie season.

'Familiarity a strength for us': Enzo Deligny on re-signing with Van Amersfoort Racing

Wheldon aiming to ‘fight for the championship’ in debut F3 season

With a lot of the confirmed grid for next year being new drivers at a new team, the 19-year-old is hopeful that familiarity will be to his and Rodin’s advantage.

“I’m excited to continue with the same team, the same car crew, and not changing much the team around me,” Clerot continued. “I'm just excited and looking forward to the fight.

Clerot is aiming for the title in 2027 after finishing sixth this year

“I do think it's an advantage to continue with the same team, especially with Rodin. It just helps, because you don't have to get used to new things, and new procedures.

“You can just continue building where you left off and we left off on a really good note. So now I'm just excited to get going in Bahrain.”

Clerot was speaking at the Jerez post-season test, and just before he jumped back in the car, he was asked what the goal for 2027 was. He responded: “Fight for the championship.”

title: 'Familiarity a strength for us': Enzo Deligny on re-signing with Van Amersfoort Racing
excerpt:
Enzo Deligny will return in 2027 for a second year of FIA Formula 3 and he will be remaining with Van Amersfoort Racing.

Re-signing with the Dutch squad is a big benefit according to Deligny, who says that the team was able to grow more as the season progressed.

Speaking after Barcelona post-season testing, the Frenchman spoke about his focus for 2027 and the area that he and the team will be looking to improve going into next year.

"I came to the team a bit late this year, so we took a bit more time to get to know each other. But we showed some good results already through the season, but it was a bit hard to get the consistency. I think for next year that's what we're targeting for sure.

"But I feel good with them so I'm excited to keep working with them. I think by the end of the year we were quite quick in Madrid, in Monza, some good races as well.

"So overall we showed that we can have some good races. It's just about being a bit more consistent throughout the year. But we know what we have to work on so I'm confident we can do better next year."

Deligny is back with VAR and says the team has made strides over the 2026 campaign

Deligny will be lining up alongside two new teammates next year with Yevan David moving over to VAR while Rashid Al Dhaheri will be the team's only rookie.

For the driver staying with the team, his experience working with VAR will be a positive factor, with the familiarity a strength to take into next year.

"I think it's quite a decent advantage because even this year there's only two post-season tests so you don't have a lot of time to get ready for next year.

"So already being comfortable with the team, it definitely helps. We're improving on our weak points.

"In Jerez we finished second overall and we were quite quick in Barcelona as well. So overall we're looking definitely more competitive than last year and it's been good."

Wheldon aiming to ‘fight for the championship’ in debut F3 season

2026 Champion Ugo Ugochukwu steps up to Formula 2 with Campos Racing for 2027

With post-season testing all over, drivers will now head into the winter break and get to focus on preparations for next year.

Along with some training camps, Deligny has one more race weekend to complete before fully focusing on his second F3 campaign with VAR.

"I'll do some training camps in hot places and then some in Norway, some cold Viking-style training campsnd then race in Macau as well. That'll be a fun one. Otherwise it won't be too long until we're back in F3."

title: Wheldon aiming to ‘fight for the championship’ in debut F3 season
excerpt:
Sebastian Wheldon is targeting a shot at the title in 2027 as he previewed his debut Formula 3 season with TRIDENT.

The American driver got down to work at the post-season tests in Jerez and Barcelona, and he recently shared his thoughts on his new team and car.

“I’m feeling really excited,” said Wheldon. “It’s a big step from FREC last year, so it will definitely be a new challenge and I'm really looking forward to it.

“It should be a good challenge and I'm really happy to be here with TRIDENT for this season, I’m looking forward to it.

“Already I feel right at home. Everyone is really friendly and we've been working really hard these past couple weeks to get ready for the season and as I said, I'm really looking forward to it.”

Wheldon steps up to F3 after a strong year in FREC where he finished second in the Drivers’ Championship with four victories and eight podiums in total.

The 17-year-old spent the four days learning the car he will be driving alongside fellow TRIDENT rookie Kean Nakamura-Berta – who he fought against for the title this year.

2026 Champion Ugo Ugochukwu steps up to Formula 2 with Campos Racing for 2027

‘It’s a great honour’ – Dion Gowda on stepping up to F3 with LN4 Fusion

Wheldon shared his thoughts on the Formula 3 car and also what it will be like racing alongside his new teammate.

“The car is a really big step compared to FREC,” he said. “You have the downforce and just more power from the engine. But that’s the biggest thing you feel is just probably more downforce and just less laps to do the lap time.

title: 2026 Champion Ugo Ugochukwu steps up to Formula 2 with Campos Racing for 2027
excerpt:
2026 Champion Ugo Ugochukwu has confirmed his plans for 2027, as he will step up to Formula 2 with Campos Racing next season.

The American driver won this year’s title at the final round in Madrid, winning two races, including seven podiums in total across the year.

Ugochukwu boasts an impressive record in single seaters, having also won the Formula Regional Oceania Trophy at the beginning of the year and also the 2025 Macau Grand Prix.

The 19-year-old will now step up to F2 with Campos, having helped the Spanish outfit retain the Formula 3 Teams’ title this season.

Speaking at the announcement, Ugochukwu was happy to be continuing with the team given the success they shared in 2026.

“Proud to announce I’ll be staying with Campos Racing for the 2027 FIA Formula 2 season,” said Ugochukwu. “After winning the F3 Championship together, I’m ready to take the next step and fight for more success.”

Campos Racing Team Principal Adrián Campos also added: “Ugo is an exceptionally talented driver with enormous potential. Since we started working together, we have been able to see his ability, professionalism and, above all, his continuous improvement first-hand. He is a driver who never stops learning and getting better, and that is essential when taking the next steps in a racing career. Winning the FIA Formula 3 title in our first season together is a fantastic achievement, but so is all the work behind that success and the progress he has made throughout the year.

“We are very pleased with the relationship we have built and the way we have developed together. That is why we approach his FIA Formula 2 debut in 2027 with great optimism. We know how demanding this championship is, but we firmly believe in his talent and his ability to keep progressing. We are looking forward to continuing to support him through this new challenge and working together to help him take another important step in his career.”

title: ‘It’s a great honour’ – Dion Gowda on stepping up to F3 with LN4 Fusion
excerpt:
Dion Gowda is confident that he and LN4 Fusion can be competitive in 2027, as he reflected on his new life in Formula 3.

The Indian driver is graduating to F3 after two years in FREC where he achieved several points finishes and took part in the two post-season tests in Jerez and Barcelona.

Speaking last month about the step up to the third tier, Gowda expressed his delight at the opportunity but also acknowledged the work that needs to be done.

“It’s been really good, I’ve been learning a lot,” said Gowda. “It's a step up for me. Obviously, a new car for me, new experience, and a new team as well. There’s a lot to learn, but it's going well and I think we're doing a good job.

Gowda talked about his start to life in F3 and how much he has been learning

The Indian driver is looking forward to racing around Jeddah and Monaco next season

“It’s a new team, but we've got some experienced people working behind the scenes. I'm quite confident that we should be fairly competitive going into the season.”

Gowda is looking forward to the “cool experience” of racing in Jeddah and Monaco next season but hopes the entire year can be a successful one for both him and the team.

“Obviously I'd like to win the championship,” he added. “But it is my rookie season, so we'll just learn as much as we can, take away as much as we can and just try to improve throughout the season, and take it step-by-step.”

title: ‘I feel ready for next year’ says De Palo after switching to MP for the 2027 season
excerpt:
Matteo De Palo is returning for another season in Formula 3 and is keen to bounce back from a tough rookie campaign with his new team.

The Italian has switched to MP Motorsport for the 2027 campaign, following on from a year where he finished 24th in the Standings with seven points.

But speaking at post-season testing in Jerez, where he started work with his new team, De Palo expressed his excitement for what is to come.

“I'm feeling good,” said De Palo. “We just finished now the first session with the new team and I am feeling really good.

“I’m really enjoying working with them, with the MP team, and also since I’ve been here, we’ve been working quite well together, so let's keep it up.”

De Palo says he is enjoying his time working with MP Motorsport so far ahead of the 2027 season

Looking back on 2026, De Palo’s season was affected by quite a few difficult moments, with disqualification for technical infringements costing him victory in the Silverstone Feature Race and a front row start in Monza.

Reviewing the year, the 19-year-old believes his individual performance levels were strong but his year was affected by issues outside of his control.

Rashid Al Dhaheri: 'We are working well already' as he assesses VAR post-season work

Gladysz eyeing title in 2027 as he returns to familiar settings in MP Motorsport

“If I have to be honest with you, individually I was happy about my performances,” said De Palo. “I felt like when I had the opportunity to perform, I always showed my pace, but then I had too many issues. I cannot even count them.

“The only two times that had everything clean, I don't say that I was lucky or some bad luck, but everything clean without any issues on reliability or stuff like this, I was at the front.

“So I'm happy because it's not about showing it to other people, but just to myself in such a tough year when everything seemed like it was going wrong.

De Palo was happy with his performance levels in 2026 despite the tough results

“It felt like I couldn't do anything to change it because everything was out of my control. It was good for me to show myself that I was still there and I am able to perform and to fight for the top position, like we saw in Spa and Monza qualifying.

“Unfortunately, I couldn't keep that result for technical infringements, but it was good for me to show myself that I can be there.”

‘The goal is to win’ says Nakamura-Berta ahead of rookie F3 campaign

'I'm more motivated than ever': Yevan David on joining Van Amersfoort Racing in 2027

Previewing the 2027 campaign, De Palo says his goals are clear but before the season’s start, he and MP have work to do to hit the ground running.

“Yeah of course,” said De Palo on fighting at the front. “We will have another go with MP, and I feel ready for next year.”

title: Rashid Al Dhaheri: 'We are working well already' as he assesses VAR post-season work
excerpt:
Rashid Al Dhaheri is hopeful that he can get up to speed quickly in FIA Formula 3 in 2027. Already confirmed at Van Amersfoort Racing, he is looking to learn as much as possible ahead of his full race debut in the Championship next year.

As the only rookie that's part of the 2027 Van Amersfoort's F3 lineup, Al Dhaheri is hoping to leverage his teammates' experience in the Championship.

As the Emirati driver prepares for his rookie campaign, he says he will be leaning on the team and teammates in order to have a solid foundation going into the new campaign.

"It's quite a step from last year, so it will be very exciting to get to know the team, to get things together and start working. I think the work is going in the right direction and I'm happy with the choices we've made.

"There's a lot of experience for me to gain. At this moment, it's just about learning, understanding, and using my teammates who are second-year drivers, to gain as much as I can from them, and I think at the end, the performance is there.

"So we're starting from a strong point, we just need to build from here. The lap times and the positions and the tests don't mean anything. It's just what we get out of it, which is the key. That's where our focus is.

Al Dhaheri says the team made a good start to their collaboration across the Jerez and Barcelona tests

"The team is very important, so the team will and they are giving some really good information.

"At the end of the day as well, it's important to kind of make mistakes or kind of try things now so that later in the season, you already know what's going to happen or you're able to anticipate certain things.

"Both are key, the team, the overall experience and just learning a bit from the drivers and teammates."

Having participated in both post-season test's the Van Amersfoort driver says that he has already got to grips with the biggest differences in terms of machinery at his disposal.

Gladysz eyeing title in 2027 as he returns to familiar settings in MP Motorsport

Compared to what he's driven so far, Al Dhaheri says that the F3 car presents new challenges, particularly in relation to tyres and tyre management. He says that taking care of the Pirelli rubber is a crucial element to learn.

"Driving-wise, it's a car like any other. There's four wheels, an engine and a steering wheel.

"The main difference is on the execution, how you get the job done with the warm-up of the tyres and how you can bring them into the window and actually use them in that window.

Al Dhaheri will be keeping busy over the winter break in preparation for his rookie campaign

"It's all about the tyres, that's the biggest difference. There's some tyre degradation, so it becomes a little bit more complex, but the fundamentals stay the same, which I think is positive. You just need to fine-tune them."

With a few months off now to prepare for the 2027 campaign, the Mercedes Junior Team driver is focused on maximising his winter break to be as prepared as possible for the new season.

That will include mental and physical preparations, before diving back into the data ahead of pre-season testing early next year.

"I don't really like time off, so I'll be getting as many days as possible doing something. But yeah,you want to develop physically just to make sure that you're at the right point.

"Also mentally, you need to get ready for the season, understanding what the key points to focus on are.

"Then, of course, technically, try to do a bit of sim work, really getting the ideas, studying, and then the exam starts only when you get back in the car."

title: Gladysz eyeing title in 2027 as he returns to familiar settings in MP Motorsport
excerpt:
Maciej Gladysz is returning for a second season of Formula 3 in a familiar environment, and he hopes to MP Motorsport will bring title success.

The Polish driver is set to race with MP in 2027, a team with which he has plenty of history, having driven for them in his first two seasons in single seater racing.

During that time, Gladysz finished third in the 2024 Formula Winter Series and Spanish F4 Championship.

In 2025, Gladysz and MP won the Eurocup-3 Spanish Winter Championship, and after a year away, he is delighted to back with the Dutch outfit.

“Obviously it's quite good to be back,” said Gladysz. “I used to race for the team in the Spanish F4 and Eurocup-3 championship. I know most of the people, so I'm happy to be back with them.

“I think we can score some great achievements for the 2027 season. Obviously, I will not be a rookie next year. I will, of course, have some experience and I will try to use that experience for better results.”

The Pole is hoping to use the lessons of 2026 to go even stronger next season with his new team

Gladysz enjoyed plenty of high moments in his rookie season, especially at Silverstone where he won the Feature Race.

The 18-year-old also achieved several points finishes in early part of the campaign, but struggled in the final three rounds for results, where he did not score.

Looking ahead to 2027, Gladysz says he has learned a lot from his rookie experience, especially when it comes to improving his Qualifying form.

“I think, obviously what I need to work on is quali,” he said. “Obviously, I need to work on quali performance. I think this year that was my main limiting factor.

Seewooruthun excited to step up to F3 with Rodin as he lays out goal for 2027

“I think this needs to be sorted for next year. If it gets sorted, I think we will be there fighting for big points.”

On the goal for 2027, Gladysz insists he does not want to put too much pressure on himself regarding results, although he knows what the big goal is at the end of the season.

“Well, the goal, obviously, is winning the championship,” he said. “But the first thing I want to focus on is to keep being consistent.

“I am not putting any pressure on myself because I want to keep enjoying it as much as possible. I hope, in the end, the result will be there, so let’s see.”

title: Seewooruthun excited to step up to F3 with Rodin as he lays out goal for 2027
excerpt:
Reza Seewooruthun is aiming for consistency in 2027 as he previewed his rookie Formula 3 season with Rodin Motorsport.

The 20-year-old makes the step up with a solid set of results in single seater racing, including a third-place finish in the 2024 British F4 Championship.

This season, Seewooruthun joined forces with Rodin in the Formula Regional European Championship, where he achieved two podiums.

As he looked ahead to next year, the British driver is delighted to be continuing with the team for this new phase of his career.

“I'm super excited to get going,” he said. “I've always wanted to race in the FIA Formula 3. I think it's one of those vital steps on the pathway, so I’m very happy to be doing it so soon.

“Continuing with Rodin just saves some of the hassle. You already know everyone, and I've also known my engineer a bit from last year, seeing him around the factory and also seeing all the boys on the sim, so it just helps the integration process be a lot smoother.

“Also, I know how the sim works and things like that, so you're not learning new things, so it's not as much compared to if I was to change teams.”

Seewooruthun is the lone rookie in a team that has Pedro Clerot and Alessandro Giusti, two drivers who have had plenty of success in Formula 3.

Speaking at testing, Seewooruthun says he was learning a lot from his teammates, looking over their data to see where he can improve.

“I think just using their data as much as I can,” said Seewooruthun on working with Clerot and Giusti. “It's always good to have fast teammates because it's vital information for me.

“Obviously, they're in their second and third year, so it's just perfect for me. I've got lots of data to go off. I can pester them for information on stuff. Again, it just makes my life a lot easier moving up, makes that process a lot easier.”

‘The goal is to win’ says Nakamura-Berta ahead of rookie F3 campaign

Looking more on the track for next season, Seewooruthun picked out the tracks he was most excited to visit and also set out his goals for each race weekend.

“I think just consistently finishing in the top ten,” said Seewooruthun on his goals for 2026. “We know how up and down these championships can be.

“By just finishing inside the top ten, you're within reach of the championship, so I’ve just got to make sure we're there for both races and then.

“I think Jeddah will be cool, or Montreal. Street circuits will be cool, especially with these cars, they're so nice to drive. There's so much traction, lots of downforce, so any of the high-speed tracks I think will be good.”

title: ‘The goal is to win’ says Nakamura-Berta ahead of rookie F3 campaign
excerpt:
Kean Nakamura-Berta is targeting a fight for the championship in 2027 as he recently previewed his rookie campaign in Formula 3.

The British driver steps up with a strong single seater resume having won the 2025 Italian F4 and Euro 4 Championships and the 2026 Formula Regional Middle East Trophy.

Most recently, Nakamura-Berta finished third in the Formula Regional European Championship and was in Jerez and Barcelona testing with his new team TRIDENT ahead of next season.

“I'm super, super excited to get the season started,” he said. “Of course joining a team like TRIDENT with a vast history of winning in the championship and looking so strong, it's a really good place to start.

“F3 is a massive jump from the lower categories. It's the first time you're on an F1 weekend and it's a really surreal experience. But I think I'm in the right place, I have good people around me and I can't wait to start.”

Nakamura-Berta has had four days of running in the F3 car and made a fast start in Jerez, ending Day 1 with the quickest time.

When asked for his impressions of the car, the 18-year-old revealed the key areas he has to adapt too in the cockpit.

“The Formula 3 has a lot more power, and a lot more downforce,” he added. “The tyres interact in a different way compared to Formula Regional.

“But it's super, super fun to drive. I am loving every minute of it, every second.”

Nakamura-Berta will be driving with TRIDENT for the first time in his career although he does have experience racing for an Italian team.

'I'm more motivated than ever': Yevan David on joining Van Amersfoort Racing in 2027

The Williams Driver Academy member says life is good so far in his new home, shining a light on how well he has been treated by everyone within the team.

“They've been incredibly welcoming,” he said. “Of course, they are Italian, but they are from different parts of Italy.

“But they've embraced me nicely and the people here are amazing. They have loads of experience, all the engineers. Of course, Giacomo running the team is really good at managing people and on that side of things."

On the goal for 2027, Nakamura-Berta is keen to do what he has done in each year of his career, fighting for victories and championships.

“Well, I think the goal for everyone is to win the championship,” he said. “So hopefully we can fight for it. I think that's the goal.”

title: 'I'm more motivated than ever': Yevan David on joining Van Amersfoort Racing in 2027
excerpt:
Yevan David will return for another season in FIA Formula 3 after confirmation he's signed with Van Amersfoort Racing for 2027.

After getting his first days of on-track running with the team in Barcelona, The Sri Lankan driver gave his thoughts on signing with the team and his early experience with the team across the post-season test.

"Very, very excited. Honestly, this is one of the most complete years I've had in a long time," David said. "To back it up with going to Van Amersfoort for 2027, I couldn't be more excited.

"Obviously, an incredible calendar that we're going to have. Really excited to go to the new tracks like Jeddah, Montreal, and Istanbul. I'm honestly just very excited to execute to the fullest.

"I absolutely love the team. A lot of different personalities. I really like my crew around me. Patrik, Tomas, they're my mechanics from Scandinavia. So I've got a cool background there.

"And then my engineer, Daniel, he's from the UK. So a lot in common with the three of us and we're really working together. And then the team itself, all the other mechanics and engineers in the team.

"I'm very much looking forward to getting to know everyone. I really feel a good energy within the team."

David was on track for the first time with VAR at the Barcelona test

David will of course have a full year of F3 experience on which to rely upon next season, something that he feels will make a big difference next year.

From understanding how the sessions evolve to general experience around each of the returning venues next year, David says he's optimistic the lessons of this season will make a difference.

"Super useful because you can see how procedures work, how the track evolves on a weekend and just basically how to put a lap together in qualifying under pressure.

"Once you've got conditioned into doing that, you know what to expect for next season. Not only that, you're not really shooting in the dark how you are in your rookie season.

Rivera: Preparations in Jerez and Barcelona show improvement in 2026

Kato pleased with ART Grand Prix work after finishing Barcelona test fastest of all

"You know exactly what to work on and how to work on it effectively. So it's a double bonus for sure."

Looking ahead to the off season, David says that the hard work has only just begun. Following the final post-season test of the year in Barcelona, the VAR driver says that he will turn his focus onto himself, making improvements as much as possible for 2027.

Having achieved a maiden podium in F3, he has his sights set on a first F3 victory in 2027.

The Sri Lankan is aiming for a maiden win in the Championship next season

"I want to win. That's exactly what I think about when I wake up in the morning and I go to sleep.

"In terms of process and in terms of what I'm focused on, it's obviously about winning but more about the process and everything behind it. I'm not going to be thinking about the lap time that I'm going to get in qualifying.

"I'm going to think about what corners I can maximise and how I can maximise the lap itself. And then everything else will follow.

"I have never been more excited to just work as hard as possible every day. Every day of mine is going to be structured to the minute for how I can work towards my goal.

"It's going to be a lot of studying the races from this year, a lot of driving on the simulator, whether it's at home or at the factory, and a lot about learning how to cope under pressure even better.

"I think once I get to a level where I know how to drive without anything being able to phase me already on building and what I have is the goal, so everything in November, December is just going to be working towards that goal."

title: Slow living at home, cameras and cooking: Behind the Visor with Kanato Le
excerpt:
Hitech's Kanato Le has been confirmed for another season in FIA Formula 3 in 2027, but outside of the race track, what does he get up to in his spare time?

Unwinding after a race weekend can be tricky, but Le says he has plenty of hobbies to choose form in order to unwind and decompress.

"When I'm away from the racetrack, I still like to go on my sim quite a bit. But I think if it's nothing related to racing, I quite like to go on a run or cycle also.

"I do bouldering as well. I like rock climbing. So I enjoy that. Since I'm living on my own, I like cooking my own food as well.

"Recently, I started doing a bit of videography. I used to do quite a bit of photography. So I have all the stuff. When I was scrolling on Instagram, I always see some cool videography, cinematography stuff. And I just wanted to give it a try and it's been pretty nice.

"I think the most recent thing I've done was when I was in Austria. Since I had a free day on the Wednesday, we went to a pretty nice place with a lake and some mountains.

"I was just recording some nature stuff. And I think it's really nice just kind of being in that relaxed environment in nature and taking some videos.

"I think I'm quite used to it by now, living by myself. I've been living on my own since 2022. Before that I was in a boarding house. But, it's quite nice. You get some freedom, peace and quiet by yourself.

"You can do whatever you want. I can cook my own food and do whatever, whenever without having to think about other people. I'm quite good at carbonara. It's pretty nice and I really enjoy it.

Rivera: Preparations in Jerez and Barcelona show improvement in 2026

Kato pleased with ART Grand Prix work after finishing Barcelona test fastest of all

"In general, I think it takes maybe one or two days just to fully reset after a race weekend. I think it's important to kind of move on after a weekend and just switch off completely.

"I think it's pretty nice just living on my own because I can just chill and just do whatever I want. Go and listen to music or go on a run or whatever. In that sense, I think it really helps me to switch off."

title: Rivera: Preparations in Jerez and Barcelona show improvement in 2026
excerpt:
Ernesto Rivera was at and near the top of the timing sheets throughout much of the two-day post-season test in Barcelona this week.

The Campos Racing driver reflected on the event afterwards and said that it had been a useful few days along with the previous test in Jerez.

The Red Bull Junior Team member said that he was able to begin his preparations for next year with confidence, and already could tell where lessons had been learned from his rookie campaign.

"They've been quite important. Before Jerez, I hadn't been in the car since Madrid, so it was good to jump back in, trying to prepare as best as possible for next year and to learn from what we did wrong this year."

Fastest in the afternoon session on the first day around the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, Rivera was positive about the work he and Campos carried out and could tell experience was making an impact.

The Mexican driver added that with the 2027 F3 season being the first time he will compete in the same Championship in consecutive seasons, he is learning as he goes with the team on how best to use that advantage.

"The track was quite fast in the afternoon and I did a good lap on the new tyres and was able to go fastest. The car felt quite good, so overall, happy with the day.

Rivera is focused on his post-season preparations for what will be his second year in FIA F3 in 2027

"It's quite different now with a year's worth of experience, especially in these types of sessions where you only have one push to lap and you can really see the experience.

"Now you know a bit more, how things should be, you have a bit more confidence. You can maybe force it a bit more if you don't feel super confident with the car.

"Just with experience, you are able to put in a good lap. It's my first time doing a second year in a category, so it's a new thing for me."

Kato pleased with ART Grand Prix work after finishing Barcelona test fastest of all

With testing over and the 2026 campaign officially in the books, Rivera and the rest of the F3 field turn attentions to the winter break.

The Campos driver says he will be heading home for the break but is looking to stay sharp with some karting, though rest will also be important in the coming months.

"I will go to Mexico, try to relax for some time, maybe do a bit of karting there with my team. I'm just trying to reset mentally and go again for next year."

title: De Palo: 'Positive early days' with MP Motorsport with Italian fastest in Barcelona
excerpt:
Matteo De Palo set the pace on Day 1 in Barcelona, logging a 1:28.516 to lead the pack on the penultimate day of on-track action in 2026.

The MP Motorsport driver topped the times in the morning session and was very pleased with his and the team's work across the entirety of the day.

Reflecting on it all after the session, De Palo said that while they couldn't read too much into times, the atmosphere within the team was already very positive.

"I'm pretty happy because I feel really good with this new team. I think the work we're doing together with MP is really nice, and that's shown today on the timing screens. So it's pretty good to see.

"But, it's still testing. So we still have to work hard for the first race of next season. But, there are really positive vibes. I'm pretty happy about how it's going, how it went in Jerez too. So we'll just keep going on like this."

Diving deeper into the relationship between driver and team, De Palo says that it is a crucial factor at this point as both learn how to work best with one another.

He added that it allows more focus to go into going quickly, something that he was able to show handidly across the opening day of action in Barcelona.

"It's almost everything at this stage because you really have to feel good with yourself and have everything in your control. There are not many chances in this championship, we just got one lap in quali and that's it. So everything has to be perfect."

Looking ahead to the final day of on-track running this year, the MP driver said that he was hopeful of more pace to come, but that focus would also be on race pace and building on the positive work so far across both tests.

"There will probably be more grip, but not that much like what happened in Jerez because there was a race here last week. So there shouldn't be much of a shift from one day to the other.

De Palo fastest on Day 1 for MP Motorsport in Barcelona

"So I don't know if there will be a big improvement. We have much more work to do but you can't read too much into things, it doesnt count for too much at this stage.

"I just want to take more confidence from tomorrow because this hasn't been the best season for myself, even if was for things not under my control, it takes out a bit of confidence.

"But already from these two tests, I gained much more and I felt much better. I felt like I did when I left FREC having been fighting for wins. So it's good to have this feeling and to race with this feeling."

title: Pedro Clerot: My Ultimate Driver
excerpt:
Pedro Clerot’s preparations for the 2027 campaign have begun with the Rodin Motorsport driver having taken part in the Jerez post-season test earlier this week.

Recently, we caught up with the Brazilian to build his ultimate racing driver, and there are a few motorsport legends on Clerot’s list.

INTELLIGENCE

“That's a really good question. I'm going to say Senna. From everything I've seen from Ayrton, from his days, he was a guy that was always ahead of his time on and off track, so that's one of the big reasons why.

DRIVING IN THE WET

“Senna again. I think it's pretty straightforward. What Ayrton did in the wet was always spectacular, so I have to go with him.”

The Brazilian earmarked Ayrton Senna for his intelligence and ability in the wet

The Rodin driver picked out Norris for his smooth driving stule

SMOOTH DRIVING STYLE

“Smoothest, I'm going to say, it's difficult actually, it can be a tricky question. The smoothest driving style, I'd say Lando. He drives really clean all the time, but Oscar also does. I'll go with Lando.”

AGGRESSIVE DRIVING STYLE

“I guess this is back to Max.”

ANYTHING ELSE?

“I would put Nelson Piquet’s technical knowledge, for sure. That guy is unbelievable. title: Freddie Slater set for F1 race weekend debut with Audi in Mexico City and Sao Paulo
excerpt:
Freddie Slater will make his debut on a Formula 1 race weekend with the Audi Formula 1 Team, taking part in both the Mexico City and Sao Paulo Grands Prix Free Practice 1 sessions.

Slater had a strong season in Formula 3, fighting for the title until the final round. He finished second in the Championship with eight podiums, including a Feature Race victory in Budapest with TRIDENT.

For 2027, the 18-year-old is set to step up to FIA Formula 2 with Invicta Racing.

Before then, Slater will make his debut in F1 for Audi in Mexico, before driving in FP1 again a week later in Sao Paulo.

At the announcement, the British driver expressed how excited he was to achieve a childhood dream.

“Getting behind the wheel of a Formula One car at a Grand Prix weekend is a big moment for me and something I’ve been dreaming of since I was a kid,” said Slater. “I’ve learned a lot this year, and these Free Practice outings with Audi Revolut F1 Team will be another opportunity to keep gaining on-track experience.

“Being part of the Audi Driver Development Programme has already given me some incredible opportunities, and I am grateful for their trust and support. I’m really looking forward to getting out on track: m y focus will be on doing the best job I can, helping the team with its programme and taking as many learnings as possible from both sessions.”

Racing Director and Director of the Audi Development Programme, Allan McNish added: “We have seen Freddie making great progress throughout recent years, both on and off the track; it is the right time for Freddie to step-up. These appearances in Mexico and Brazil will give him valuable experience of a Formula One race weekend, and another chance to continue his development before he steps up to Formula 2 next season. We are looking forward to seeing him in the R26 and supporting him through these two important FP1 sessions.”

title: ‘I had a blast’ - Macedo pleased with performance after ‘unexpected’ test with VAR in Jerez
excerpt:
Francisco Macedo set the fastest time of this week’s Jerez post-season test, after receiving a late call up from Van Amersfoort Racing.

The Portuguese driver showed strong pace, recovering from some issues on Day 1 to top the timesheets on the second day’s morning session.

When times were at their quickest during the qualifying runs, Macedo completed a 1:29.766, the best time of the week, leading fellow VAR driver Enzo Deligny by 0.169s.

Macedo followed that up with a run to second in the afternoon, which was dominated by race simulations.

Speaking in the paddock at the end of the test, Macedo reflected on the unexpected opportunity to jump into the F3 car.

“It was a bit of an unexpected test,” he said. “I actually received a late call. I tried to prepare myself as best as possible, and today I managed to get a P1 in the morning, P2 in the afternoon.

Macedo set the fastest time of the test ahead of fellow VAR driver Deligny

“Unfortunately, yesterday I had some issues during the day, but me and the team managed to solve them during the night, and today we were fastest.”

Speaking further about his time driving the Formula 3 car, Macedo picked out the best parts of the experience.

“It was my first time in the F3, and it's completely different to the FREC that I am used to driving,” he explained.

“It has a lot more speed, a lot better braking, and I just had a blast. VAR was my team from last year, so it was quite easy to adapt to that aspect.

“I already knew everyone and I felt very comfortable since day one with the team and of course with the car too.”

Macedo talked about adapting to the Formula 3 car and how much he enjoyed the experience

Speaking more about the challenges that he had to adapt to, Macedo picked out tyre management on race runs, especially with there being two different compounds this week – the Medium and the Hard.

“It was a big challenge because in my previous categories, it was always a one-compound tyre,” he explained.

When asked if he had adapted well to the tyres by the end, Macedo joked: “Actually I managed to survive at least to the end.”

title: Francisco Macedo fastest on Day 2 of Jerez Post-Season test for Van Amersfoort Racing

Once the action resumed, Ernesto Rivera went to P1 on a 1:31.584. But there were several more improvements to come, with Taito Kato leading Keanu Al Ahzari by 0.003s with a 1:31.463.

Dion Gowda then went fastest with a 1:30.935 before improving to a 1:30.860, putting 0.169s between he and teammate James Egozi.

Al Azhari briefly went top with a 1:30.700, before Mattia Colnaghi eclipsed that time by 0.029s.

Kato was flying and completed an eye-catching 1:30.386 to put 0.266s between he and Rivera.

Niccolò Maccagnani then lowered the time to beat to a 1:30.302 with just over 90 minutes to go in the session.

Moments later, the Red Flags were waved with Francisco Macedo having stopped on track at Turn 8. But once the action resumed Colnaghi retook his place at the top with a 1:30.037.

The Argentinian driver was over two-and-a half tenths clear of the rest, although Jin Nakamura reduced the gap to 0.136s.

As the second hour of running came to an end, Enzo Deligny became the first to go into the 1:29s. The Van Amersfoort Racing driver’s 1:29.935 put him on top by 0.017s to Clerot. Macedo then made it a VAR 1-2, going fastest on a 1:29.766.

Into the final hour, and race runs were the focus for the majority, although with 30 minutes to go, there was a Red Flag. Maciej Gladysz found the gravel at Turn 5.

Running resumed, but there were no further changes to the timesheets, leaving Macedo on top ahead of Deligny, Clerot, Reza Seewooruthun, and Colnaghi.

AFTERNOON

After missing most of the morning session, Giusti returned to the track in the afternoon, and completed a 1:30.322 to lead the way.

Long runs were the focus for the teams after that, although there was a stoppage with just under two hours to go with Miguel Costa having stopped at the pit entry.

Once the lights turned green, practice starts and race simulations were still on the agenda, meaning there were no improvements to the timesheets.

Giusti ended up on top ahead of Macedo, Nakamura, Alex Powell and Nandhavud Bhirombhakdi.

That wraps up the Jerez post-season test but the drivers will be back out on track in Barcelona from October 26-27.

title: Nakamura-Berta reflects on ‘big learning day’ after ending up fastest in Jerez
excerpt:
Kean Nakamura-Berta was happy with how things went on the opening day of running in Jerez

Kean Nakamura-Berta hailed a productive opening day of post-season testing in Jerez, with the TRIDENT driver ending up at the top of the leaderboard.

The British rookie showed good pace throughout the day before going to the top of the timesheets late in the afternoon session.

Nakamura-Berta’s 1:31.169 put him on top by 0.002s to Campos Racing’s Mattia Colnaghi, with Ernesto Rivera rounding out the top three – 0.011s off the leading time.

Speaking in the paddock after debriefing with the team, Nakamura-Berta reflected on a positive day of running in Jerez.

“Overall it was a very productive day,” he said. “We were learning loads of new stuff with this new car, and obviously the jump to F3 is massive, so it's just been a big learning day.

“Obviously tomorrow will be as well, and so will Barcelona next week. But it's been really, really fun to drive around here.

Nakamura-Berta was happy with a productive first day of running in Formula 3

“The track is insane, it's super fun, and it's challenging in parts, heavy braking, high speed as well. So it's really good to develop and then understand how to drive the car.

“Everyone's testing different things and different run plans, but I think it's been positive. The pace definitely doesn't look too shabby. But there's loads to improve on and work on as well, so we just keep going forwards.”

AS IT HAPPENED: Follow the action on Day 1 of post-season testing in Jerez

PREVIEW: 2026 Post-Season Testing starts with two days in Jerez

When asked what his takeaways were about the Formula 3 car after one day of running, Nakamura-Berta spoke about the different things he has to learn and adapt too.

“One lap on the peak to get the tyre into that working optimal temperature is quite difficult,” he explained. “That's been a key thing for me, at least today.

“I really struggled the majority of the day to do it, and towards the end we started to find a good rhythm. But I definitely still need to work on a lot of things to improve and work on.

Nakamura-Berta was happy with how he and TRIDENT worked together on Day 1

“But it's been a really solid first day. The team have been incredible, and we have worked really well, so we just keep going.”

Looking ahead to Day 2 in Jerez, Nakamura-Berta and TRIDENT still have a few tyres remaining, and while chasing fast times is fun, he says the focus will remain on improving further in the car.

“We have tyres left, we have Mediums left, we also have Hards left,” said Nakamura-Berta. “So we'll just keep on our plan, we'll just keep working within ourselves internally.

“We’ve got incredible data from the past, loads of really strong drivers have come through this team, so we've got good data there to compare too.

“So that's what we'll just be comparing to, and we will just have a little glance at the timesheets once in a while, but it’s mainly about working inside and just trying to learn as much as possible before the season starts.”

title: Nakamura-Berta ends Day 1 of Jerez post-season testing on top
excerpt:
Kean Nakamura-Berta ended Day 1 of the Jerez post-season test on top for TRIDENT.

The British driver completed a 1:31.169 in the afternoon session to top the times, with Campos Racing’s Ernesto Rivera having led the way in the morning with a 1:31.217.

MORNING

It was a quiet first part of the day as installation laps took priority with the drivers and teams looking to get everything in order before hitting the track for their flying laps.

As the first 90 minutes of the day came to an end, AIX Racing sent their three drivers out for the flying laps of the day.

James Egozi completed a 1:34.526 before improving to a 1:32.680 on his next attempt. On each occasion, he was over seven-tenths quicker than teammate Dion Gowda.

MP Motorsport’s Matteo De Palo then beat that time with a 1:32.353. The Italian clocked a 1:31.867 on his next lap, with Maciej Gladysz going to P2 – 0.582s down on his teammate.

Hitech’s Kanato Le cut the gap down to De Palo to just 0.105s with DAMS Lucas Oil’s Miguel Costa going up to P3.

On his next lap, Costa took over at the top by 0.038s, completing a 1:31.829 to cap a solid start to the test.

Teams’ champions Campos Racing then made their first move of the day, as Ernesto Rivera went quickest on a 1:31.217 on a new set of Mediums. Teammate Mattia Colnaghi was second, over three-tenths behind.

With 15 minutes left in the session, Enzo Deligny moved up to P2, 0.188s down on Rivera.

There were no further improvements in the session, with Rivera remaining on top ahead of Deligny, Colnaghi, Alessandro Giusti and Alexander Abkhazava.

AFTERNOON

Rivera picked up where he left off in the morning to set the fastest time of a 1:31.784. However, he was quickly demoted to P2 by TRIDENT’s Niccolò Maccagnani on a 1:31.632.

Long runs then became the focus for the teams, although we did see a few improvements as Rashid Al Dhaheri went up to fourth ahead of Taito Kato.

Costa continued his fine form with DAMS by going up to third with just over 45 minutes left in the session, 0.293s away from Maccagnani.

As the session approached its final stages, a few teams put on a set of new Hard tyres, and with that Kean Nakamura-Berta went top on a 1:31.169.

Maccagnani followed him across the line moments later to go up to P2, making it a TRIDENT 1-2, with the Italian driver just 0.044s away from his teammate.

Colnaghi then made a late move up the leaderboard for Campos, going to within 0.002s off Nakamura-Berta, with Rivera in P3, just 0.011s away from the leading time.

Heading into the final few minutes, DAMS Lucas Oil’s Abkhazava, stopped on track, with the session unable to start before the chequered flag was waved.

That wraps up Day 1 in Jerez, with Nakamura-Berta on top ahead of Colnaghi, Rivera, Maccagnani and Giusti. Egozi was sixth, ahead of Taito Kato, De Palo, Sebastian Wheldon, and Emmanuele Olivieri.

The drivers will be back out on track for the final day of testing in Jerez at 09:00 local time tomorrow morning.
